english: Iccius, the blessed now of the Arabs you envy
note: beatis ... gazis spans lines 1-2; invides + dative: you cast envious eyes on.

english: treasures, and fierce warfare you prepare
for the not before conquered of Sabaea
note: non ante devictis ... regibus spans lines 3-4: kings never before conquered.

english: kings, and for the dreadful Mede
you weave chains? Which to you of the maidens,
note: nectis catenas: literally 'weave chains', i.e. forge fetters for captives.

english: her betrothed slain, barbarian, will be a slave,
note: sponso necato ablative absolute; barbara agrees with quae (the maiden). 'her' supplied.

english: what boy from the court, with hair
at the ladle will be stationed, anointed,
note: ad cyathum statuetur: will be set at the ladle, i.e. made cupbearer.

english: taught to stretch Seric arrows
note: Sericas: of the Seres (the Chinese); tendere sagittas: aim/shoot arrows.

english: with the paternal bow? Who would deny that to the steep
downward streams can slide back
mountains, and the Tiber turn back,
when you, bought up from everywhere, the noble
note: coemptos ... libros spans 13-14; nobilis agrees with Panaeti (genitive).

english: books of Panaetius and the Socratic house
to exchange for Hiberian breastplates,
note: mutare + ablative: give in exchange for; Hiberis = Spanish.

english: having promised better things, are intent?
O Venus, queen of Cnidos and Paphos,
spurn beloved Cypros and, of her calling
note: vocantis ... Glycerae: of Glycera, who calls you.

english: you with much incense, of Glycera, the comely
transfer into the shrine.
note: transfer: imperative with te (line 3) as object: carry yourself over.

english: Let the burning boy with you, and with loosened
note: puer = Cupid; properent (line 6) governs all subjects; solutis ... zonis spans 5-6.

english: girdles the Graces, and let the Nymphs hasten,

latin: et parum comis sine te Iuventas
english: and, little gracious without you, Youth
note: parum comis: hardly gracious; Iuventas personified (Youth, Hebe).

english: and Mercury.
What from the dedicated Apollo asks
note: poscit with double accusative; dedicatum refers to the newly consecrated temple of Apollo (28 BC).

latin: vates? quid orat de patera novum
english: the bard? What does he pray, from the bowl new
note: novum ... liquorem spans lines 2-3: new wine poured in libation.

english: liquid pouring? Not the rich
note: opimae read as nom. pl. with segetes; it could also be gen. with Sardiniae.

english: crops of fertile Sardinia,
not of sweltering Calabria the pleasing

latin: armenta, non aurum aut ebur Indicum,
english: herds, not gold or Indian ivory,
not the fields which the Liris with quiet
water gnaws, the silent river.
Let them prune with the Calenian sickle, those to whom has given
note: premant: check, prune; 'those' supplied as antecedent of quibus.

english: Fortune the vine, so that, rich, from golden
the merchant may drain cups
the wines got in exchange for Syrian merchandise,
note: reparata: acquired in exchange (Syra merce, ablative).

latin: dis carus ipsis, quippe ter et quater
english: dear to the gods themselves, since three and four times
in a year revisiting the Atlantic sea
unharmed. Me olives feed,
me chicory and light mallows.
To enjoy things acquired, and healthy, to me,
note: paratis: what has been gained; valido agrees with mihi.

english: son of Leto, may you grant, and, I pray, with sound
note: Latoe: vocative, Apollo son of Leto; integra ... mente spans 18-19.

english: mind, neither a shameful old age
to pass nor one lacking the cithara.

latin: Poscimur. si quid vacui sub umbra
english: We are summoned. If anything, at leisure, under the shade
note: Poscimur: some MSS read Poscimus ('we ask'); passive kept. vacui: nom. pl., free/at leisure.

latin: lusimus tecum, quod et hunc in annum
english: we have played with you, which both into this year

latin: vivat et pluris, age dic Latinum,
english: may live and more, come, speak a Latin,
barbitos, song,
note: barbite: vocative of barbitos, the lyre addressed.

english: first tuned by a Lesbian citizen,
note: Alcaeus of Lesbos; modulate is vocative, agreeing with barbite.

latin: qui ferox bello tamen, inter arma
english: who, fierce in war, nevertheless, amid arms
or if the tossed he had tied up on the wet
note: iactatam ... navim spans 7-8; sive: or if (he had moored).

english: shore ship,

latin: Liberum et Musas Veneremque et illi
english: Liber and the Muses and Venus and, to her,
always clinging, the boy, used to sing,
note: puerum = Cupid; canebat: imperfect, used to sing.

english: and Lycus, with black eyes and black
note: Lycus: a boy loved by Alcaeus.

english: hair handsome.

latin: o decus Phoebi et dapibus supremi
english: O glory of Phoebus and, at the feasts of the highest
pleasing tortoise-shell of Jupiter, O of toils
note: testudo: tortoise(-shell), i.e. the lyre; metaphor kept.

english: sweet soothing, to me, whenever, hail
note: mihi cumque is textually doubtful (emendations medicumque, mihi cuique); literal 'to me whenever' kept.

english: duly calling!

latin: Albi, ne doleas plus nimio memor
english: Albius, do not grieve more than too much, mindful
note: plus nimio: more than too much, i.e. excessively.

english: of harsh Glycera, nor pitiful
chant elegies, why to you a younger man
outshines, faith having been injured.
note: laesa fide: ablative absolute, her faith broken.

english: Notable for her low forehead, Lycoris
note: tenui fronte: narrow/low forehead, a mark of beauty.

latin: Cyri torret amor, Cyrus in asperam
english: love of Cyrus scorches; Cyrus towards harsh
turns aside, Pholoe; but sooner to Apulian
will be joined roe-deer wolves
note: Proverbial impossibility; capreae subject, lupis dative (to wolves).

english: than Pholoe sin with a base adulterer.

latin: sic visum Veneri, cui placet inpares
english: So it has seemed good to Venus, whom it pleases unequal

latin: formas atque animos sub iuga aenea
english: forms and minds under yokes bronze
note: sub iuga aenea: under bronze yokes.

english: with cruel jest to send.

latin: ipsum me melior cum peteret Venus,
english: Myself, when a better Venus was seeking me,
note: ipsum me; Venus = love; 'me' expressed once in the Latin, English keeps 'myself ... me'.

english: with a welcome shackle held fast Myrtale
the freedwoman, fiercer than the straits of Hadria
curving the Calabrian bays.
A sparing and infrequent worshipper of the gods,
while of a mad wisdom
an expert I wander, now backwards
to give sails and to repeat courses
I am compelled, abandoned: for Diespiter,
note: relictos agrees with cursus (courses abandoned); Diespiter = Jupiter.

english: with flashing fire the clouds dividing
mostly, through the clear sky the thundering
note: per purum: through the clear (sky), 'sky' supplied; tonantis agrees with equos.

english: drove horses and swift chariot,

latin: quo bruta tellus et vaga flumina,
english: by which the dull earth and the wandering rivers,

latin: quo Styx et invisi horrida Taenari
english: by which Styx and of hated Taenarus the dreadful
seat and the Atlantean boundary
is shaken. He has power the lowest with the highest
note: valet: is able; subject deus in line 13.

english: to exchange, and the conspicuous makes faint, the god,
bringing forth the obscure; from here the crest rapacious
note: apicem: crest, a symbol of rank; rapax agrees with Fortuna (line 15) despite the source's colon.

english: Fortune with shrill whirring
note: stridore: whir of wings (Fortune as a bird of prey).

english: has carried off, here delights to have set it.

latin: O diva, gratum quae regis Antium,
english: O goddess, who rule pleasing Antium,

latin: praesens vel imo tollere de gradu
english: present either from the lowest step to raise
a mortal body or proud
to turn triumphs into funerals:
you the poor with anxious prayer courts,
tenant of the countryside, you, mistress of the sea,
note: te dominam aequoris: object of ambit understood from line 5 (whoever ... courts you as mistress of the sea).

english: whoever with Bithynian provokes
the Carpathian sea, keel;

latin: te Dacus asper, te profugi Scythae
english: you the rough Dacian, you the fugitive Scythians,
and cities and peoples and fierce Latium
and of kings the mothers, of barbarian, and
purple tyrants fear,
lest with injurious foot you overthrow
the standing column, or the people thronging
note: Column: metaphor for the state's stability; kept.

english: to arms, the idle to arms
rouse and the empire break;
you always goes before savage Necessity,
note: te object, Necessitas subject: Necessity goes before you.

english: beam-spikes and wedges in hand
note: manu ... aena spans 18-19: in bronze hand.

english: carrying, bronze, nor the stern
hook is absent and the liquid lead;
note: uncus: clamp/hook; instruments of fixing (or torture).

latin: te Spes et albo rara Fides colit
english: you Hope and, in white, rare Faith cultivates,
note: albo ... panno spans 21-22; colit singular with two subjects.

english: veiled, cloth, nor denies herself as companion,
whenever with changed of the powerful
garment the houses, hostile, you leave,

latin: at volgus infidum et meretrix retro
english: but the faithless crowd and the harlot back
perjured withdraws, scatter, the jars
with dregs drained, the friends,
to bear the yoke equally treacherous:
note: ferre iugum pariter dolosi: too faithless to share the yoke (of misfortune); yoke metaphor kept.

english: may you keep Caesar, about to go against the farthest
of the world Britons, and of young men the fresh
note: recens examen: new swarm (levy); metaphor kept.

english: swarm, to be feared by the Eastern
regions and by the red Ocean.
note: Oceanus ruber: Red Sea / Persian Gulf region.

latin: heu heu, cicatricum et sceleris pudet
english: Alas, alas, of scars and of crime it shames
and of brothers. What have we, hard, shrunk from,
note: nos dura ... aetas spans 34-35: we, a hard age.

english: age? What untouched, of wickedness,
have we left? From what has the youth its hand
through fear of the gods held back? Which
altars has it spared? O would that on a new
anvil you might reforge the blunted, against
note: diffingas: forge anew; retusum ... ferrum spans 39-40.

english: the Massagetae and Arabs, iron.
Both with incense and with strings it pleases
to appease and with a calf's owed blood
note: vituli sanguine debito: with the vowed blood of a calf.

english: the guardian gods of Numida,

latin: qui nunc Hesperia sospes ab ultima
english: who now from farthest Hesperia, safe,
to dear comrades many,
to none more, nevertheless, will distribute kisses
than to sweet Lamia, mindful
of a boyhood passed under no other king
note: non alio rege: not under another king (schoolmaster or leader of boys' games); negative kept.

english: and of the toga changed at the same time.
note: The assumption of the toga virilis.

latin: Cressa ne careat pulcra dies nota
english: Let not lack a Cretan, beautiful, the day, mark,
note: Cressa ... nota: Cretan (white chalk) mark for a lucky day.

english: nor of the brought-out amphora a limit

latin: neu morem in Salium sit requies pedum
english: nor in the Salian manner let there be rest of feet,
nor let much-unmixed-wine Damalis
note: multi ... meri: genitive of quality, Damalis of much neat wine.

english: Bassus with Thracian amystis conquer,
note: amystis: draining a cup in one breath, a Thracian practice.

english: nor let roses be lacking to the feasts

latin: neu vivax apium neu breve lilium.
english: nor long-lived parsley nor short-lived lily.
All upon Damalis melting
will set their eyes, nor Damalis from the new
will be torn away adulterer,
than wanton ivies more clinging.

latin: Nunc est bibendum, nunc pede libero
english: Now is to be drunk, now with free foot
to be struck the earth; now with Salian
note: Saliaribus ... dapibus spans 2-4: feasts worthy of the Salii, i.e. lavish.

english: to adorn the couch of the gods
note: pulvinar: cushioned couch for the gods' images (lectisternium).

english: it was time with feasts, comrades.
Before this it was wrong to bring out Caecuban
from ancestral cellars, while for the Capitol
a queen mad ruins
note: dementis ruinas: transferred epithet, acc. pl.; regina = Cleopatra.

english: and death for the empire was preparing
with a polluted herd of foul
with disease men, anything unrestrained
note: morbo: by disease (vice); impotens + infinitive: unrestrained enough to.

english: to hope and with fortune sweet
drunk. But lessened her frenzy

latin: vix una sospes navis ab ignibus
english: scarcely one ship safe from the fires
and her mind crazed with Mareotic
drove back into true fears
Caesar, from Italy her flying
with oars pressing hard, as a hawk
soft doves or the hare a swift
hunter in the fields of snowy
Haemonia, so that he might give to chains
the fated monster. She, more nobly
note: quae: feminine, refers to the queen despite monstrum (neuter).

english: seeking to perish, neither womanishly
feared the sword, nor hidden
with swift fleet gained in exchange shores.
note: reparavit: obtained in exchange; textually some read penetravit.

english: Having dared even to look on her palace lying
with serene face, brave also, rough
to handle serpents, so that black
with her body she might drink up poison,
by deliberate death more fierce;
the savage Liburnians, evidently, begrudging
note: Liburnis: dative with invidens; Liburnian galleys.

english: to be led down, a private woman, to proud,
not a humble woman, triumph.
Persian I hate, boy, trappings,
displease, woven with linden-bark, garlands,
cease to seek in which of places the rose
late lingers.
To simple myrtle that you add nothing with toil
earnest I care: neither you, as servant,
note: sedulus: (I) earnestly, or (you) officious; ambiguity kept.

latin: dedecet myrtus neque me sub arta
english: does myrtle misbecome nor me, beneath a close
vine drinking.
The civil commotion from Metellus consul
note: 60 BC, consulship of Q. Metellus Celer.

latin: bellique causas et vitia et modos
english: and of war the causes and faults and modes
and the game of Fortune and the heavy
note: gravis ... amicitias: grave (ominous) friendships of the leaders.

english: friendships of the leaders and arms
smeared with not yet expiated bloodshed,
a work full of dangerous dice,
you handle, and you walk through fires
placed beneath deceitful ash.
note: Metaphor kept: danger hidden under seeming calm.

english: A little, of severe tragedy let the Muse
be absent from the theatres: soon when public
affairs you have set in order, the great office
note: publicas res: public affairs (history); ordinaris = ordinaveris.

english: with Cecropian buskin you will resume,
distinguished protection for sorrowful defendants
and for the consulting, Pollio, senate-house,
for whom the laurel eternal honours
by Dalmatian triumph brought forth.
Already now with menacing murmur of horns
you graze ears, already the clarions blare,
note: perstringis: you strike, deafen; lituus: curved trumpet.

english: already the gleam of arms the fleeing
terrifies horses and of riders the faces.
note: fugacis equos: horses ready to flee.

english: To hear great already I seem leaders,
with not unseemly dust soiled,
and all of the lands subdued
except the fierce spirit of Cato.
Juno and whoever of the gods more friendly
to the Africans, unavenged, had withdrawn powerless
note: inulta ... tellure: from the land unavenged.

english: from the land, of the victors the grandsons
has offered back as funeral sacrifices to Jugurtha.
note: rettulit inferias: brought back as offerings to the dead.

english: What not with Latin blood more fertile
field with graves the impious battles
attests, and, heard by the Medes,
of Hesperia the sound of ruin?

latin: qui gurges aut quae flumina lugubris
english: What whirlpool or what rivers of mournful
ignorant war? What sea Daunian
have not discoloured slaughters?
What shore lacks blood ours?

latin: sed ne relictis, Musa procax, iocis
english: But lest, abandoned, Muse saucy, jests,
of Cean you take up again the offices dirge,
note: Ceae ... neniae: the Cean dirge (Simonides of Ceos); munera: functions, offices.

english: with me in a Dionean cave
note: Dionaeo: of Dione, Venus's mother, i.e. of love.

english: seek measures with a lighter plectrum.
